title: Three perfect days in Los Angeles: Venice, the Sunset Strip and downtown
dek: A free Sheryl Crow show closes the Sunset Strip to cars, MOCA opens two new exhibitions on Sunday, and Venice is at its quietest in mid-November. Here is how to fit it all into one weekend.

hero.caption: The Hollywood Sign on Mount Lee, seen on Saturday morning from the lawn at Lake Hollywood Park.

intro:
Mid-November is a good time to see Los Angeles. The summer crowds are long gone, the light is low and gold by mid-afternoon, and the forecast calls for highs in the upper 70s on Friday and Saturday, though showers may arrive on Sunday. The sun sets before 5 p.m., so plan your outdoor hours early in the day.

This weekend has three big draws, and the plan is built around them. On **Saturday**, West Hollywood closes the Sunset Strip between Doheny Drive and San Vicente Boulevard for **Live on Sunset**, a free street concert from 4 p.m. to midnight. Sheryl Crow headlines, with Local Natives and Empress Of. Entry is free, but you have to register in advance. On **Sunday**, MOCA Grand Avenue opens two new exhibitions on the same day: Julian Charrière's *Deep End*, which is about the ocean, and Cecilia Vicuña's *Quipu of Encounters*. Admission to MOCA is free. Across town that weekend, Tyler, the Creator's Camp Flog Gnaw fills the grounds of Dodger Stadium, and CicLAvia closes Colorado Boulevard in Pasadena to cars for the day.

Friday is a slower day by the ocean: breakfast at a Venice bakery, the canals, Abbot Kinney Boulevard and the Museum of Jurassic Technology, then handmade pasta for dinner. Saturday goes from a diner on Franklin Avenue, past the Hollywood Sign and Hollywood Forever, to the Strip. Sunday takes you downtown on Angels Flight, through the Smorgasburg market and Little Tokyo, and ends at *Oh, Mary!*, the Broadway comedy that is playing the Ahmanson with Alaska Thunderfuck as Mary Todd Lincoln.

days.title: Friday: Venice, the canals and Culver City
days.intro: A slow day on the Westside: a bakery breakfast, the quiet canals, a museum unlike any other, and pasta for dinner a few blocks from the sand.

stops.name: Gjusta
stops.text: Gjusta is a bakery, deli and smokehouse that opens at 7 a.m. every day. Its long counter is the best breakfast in Venice. Time Out's April 2026 list recommends the banana chocolate tart, the croque madame and the tahini croissant. Add a loaf to take home, since the bread is the reason the place exists. Seating is a few tables and a back patio, so order at the counter and get a table as soon as one frees up. It closes at 4 p.m.

stops.name: Venice Canals and Abbot Kinney Boulevard
stops.text: Abbot Kinney had the canals dug in 1905 for his Venice of America. The few that are left are lined with small bungalows and modern glass houses, and the arched footbridges are open to everyone. Walk the loop between Venice Boulevard and Washington Boulevard in about half an hour, then cut north to Abbot Kinney Boulevard, the street named after him, for its bookshops, boutiques and cafés. These are homes, so keep your voice down and stay off the private docks.

stops.name: Gjelina
stops.text: Gjelina has been the main restaurant on Abbot Kinney Boulevard for years, and it is still on Time Out's 2026 list of the best restaurants in Venice. Lunch is the easiest time to get a table. Order vegetables first: the grilled oyster mushrooms and whatever escarole or chicory salad is in season. Then share a thin wood-fired pizza. You will probably sit at a communal table. It's a good place to linger before the drive inland.

stops.name: Museum of Jurassic Technology
stops.text: This small, dark museum on Venice Boulevard is hard to describe and easy to love. Its exhibits are cases of curiosities, micro-sculptures and long, earnest captions, and you're left to decide what is real and what is made up. Plan on at least ninety minutes, and go upstairs before you leave. It opens at 2 p.m. on Fridays and stays open until 8 p.m. The suggested admission is $15. Capacity is small, so reserve a timed entry online.

stops.name: Venice Beach at sunset
stops.text: Drive back to the coast in time for the sun, which sets just before 5 p.m. this week. Walk out past the Venice Beach Skatepark to the water, then north along Ocean Front Walk while the street vendors pack up and the light turns orange on the Santa Monica Mountains. Bring a layer: it cools off quickly once the sun goes down, even after a warm day.

stops.name: Felix Trattoria
stops.text: Evan Funke's trattoria is about handmade pasta: through a glass-walled room, you can watch the pasta being rolled out by hand. Time Out's April 2026 Venice list recommends the pastas and the sfincione, a Sicilian focaccia, and says to order the spaghetti with bottarga if it is on. Share a pasta course and a main between two people rather than ordering a full menu each. Book ahead, because Friday tables go first.

stops.name: Hinano Café
stops.text: Hinano Café is a beach bar a block from the sand near the Venice Pier, and it's still on Time Out's 2026 Venice list. If dinner left you hungry, order the cheeseburger with chips, which is what the place is known for. It's loud and friendly and nothing to dress up for.

days.title: Saturday: Hollywood and Live on Sunset
days.intro: A morning view of the sign and a walk among the graves of old Hollywood, then the Sunset Strip without cars for a free concert that runs until midnight.

stops.name: Clark Street Diner
stops.text: Clark Street Bread runs this diner in the old Franklin Avenue coffee-shop space, with booths and counter seats. It's a calm place to start a long day. The Infatuation's July 2026 Hollywood guide recommends the patty melt, but come early for breakfast, when the booths are easy to get. It's ten minutes by car from the Lake Hollywood lookout, so this is a good place to fuel up before the hills.

stops.name: Lake Hollywood Park
stops.text: This small grass park below Mount Lee has one of the closest views of the Hollywood Sign that you can get without a long hike. It's a lawn, not a trail, so it suits any shoes. The park has no lot, and the streets around it are steep and residential. Circle once for a space, or take a rideshare and ask to be dropped at the park. Mornings are quieter and have the best light. Zoom in for your photograph rather than climbing closer.

stops.name: Hollywood Forever Cemetery
stops.text: Hollywood Forever is still a working cemetery, behind the Paramount lot. It's also the best place to understand the film business's early years. Inside the Cathedral Mausoleum (open 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.), you'll find Rudolph Valentino's crypt. Out on the grounds, look for Douglas Fairbanks's long reflecting pool and the bronze statue of Johnny Ramone. Peacocks wander the lawns. The grounds are open from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Be respectful, since funerals still take place here.

stops.name: Mario's Peruvian & Seafood
stops.text: Mario's Peruvian is a crowded strip-mall room a few blocks south of the cemetery, and it is a Hollywood lunch standby. The Infatuation's July 2026 guide still lists it. Order the ceviche mixto and the chicharrón de calamares. Expect a short wait at the door, quick service and portions large enough to get you through a long evening on the Strip.

stops.name: Live on Sunset
stops.text: West Hollywood closes Sunset Boulevard between Doheny Drive and San Vicente Boulevard for a free concert from 4 p.m. to midnight, with food vendors along the route. Local Natives, Empress Of, Grace Bowers and DJs Doug Locke and Mia Moretti play before Sheryl Crow. Entry is free, but you need to register at liveonsunsetweho.com and bring your scannable ticket. Bags must be clear and no larger than 12 by 6 by 12 inches.

stops.name: Ladyhawk
stops.text: Step away from the stages for a proper dinner at Ladyhawk, the Lebanese restaurant in the La Peer Hotel. It's about a fifteen-minute walk down from the Strip. Time Out (March 2026) calls it "a masterclass in Levantine flavor profiles". Order the dip platters, a wood-fired flatbread and one of the roasted meats to share. It opens at 5 p.m. on Saturdays. Book an early table so you can get back to the street in time for the headliner.

stops.name: Sheryl Crow closes Live on Sunset
stops.text: Go back up to the Strip for the evening sets. The Strip is where the Whisky a Go Go, the Roxy and the Viper Room built their reputations, and with no cars on it you can walk down the middle of the boulevard. Sheryl Crow headlines, and the event runs until midnight, rain or shine. When it's over, walk east past San Vicente Boulevard or downhill toward Santa Monica Boulevard for a rideshare. Cars can't get onto the closed blocks.

days.title: Sunday: Bunker Hill, the Arts District and Little Tokyo
days.intro: MOCA's opening day, a ride on the shortest railway in the city, Sunday's food market and a 7 p.m. comedy at the Ahmanson, all downtown.

stops.name: Pine & Crane DTLA
stops.text: The downtown branch of the Silver Lake Taiwanese café is on Time Out's January 2026 list of the best breakfasts in the city. Order the purple rice fan tuan (a stuffed rice roll), the daikon rice cakes and the chive-and-egg pockets, with a warm soy milk. You order at the counter, the room is bright, and breakfast is quick and inexpensive. From here, Angels Flight is a short ride or a twenty-minute walk north on Hill Street.

stops.name: Angels Flight
stops.text: The little orange funicular has climbed Bunker Hill since 1901, and today it runs a single block from Hill Street up to California Plaza. The ride takes about a minute and saves you a steep climb. A ticket is $1.50 each way, or 75 cents with a loaded TAP card, and it runs from about 6:45 a.m. to 10 p.m. At the top, MOCA is a three-minute walk along Grand Avenue.

stops.name: MOCA Grand Avenue
stops.text: Sunday is opening day for two new MOCA exhibitions by the winners of the museum's first Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize. Julian Charrière's *Deep End* is his first museum show in Los Angeles. It includes a darkened room that evokes the deep ocean and *Hope Line*, a live feed from a bleached Jamaican coral reef. Cecilia Vicuña's *Quipu of Encounters: The Dream of Water* opens alongside it. General admission is free, and the museum is open 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Reserve a time in advance.
stops.wiki: Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles

stops.name: Smorgasburg LA
stops.text: Every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., the food market fills the grounds of ROW DTLA, an old produce terminal on Alameda Street, with dozens of vendors. Entry is free, and you pay each stall. The way to do it is to graze: walk a full lap first, then share several small plates rather than committing to one big one. A large garage is on site if you drove. If the forecast showers arrive, go early, because most of the seating is outdoors.

stops.name: Little Tokyo
stops.text: Little Tokyo is one of only three Japantowns left in the United States. Walk from the Japanese Village Plaza with its fire tower up First and Second streets, past the old Nishi Hongwanji temple building, and stop at the mochi and manju shops that have been here for generations. The Japanese American National Museum is closed for renovation until early 2027, but the street-level history is worth an hour, and the Arts District is a short walk east for dinner.

stops.name: Camphor
stops.text: Camphor, a French bistro in the Arts District, makes the case for an early dinner. Time Out's September 2026 list of the best restaurants in Los Angeles recommends the sea bream with uni, the creamy mussels with matchstick potatoes, and the citrus-milk dessert. It opens at 5 p.m. on Sundays. An early booking gives you time to get across downtown to the Music Center before curtain.

stops.name: Oh, Mary! at the Ahmanson
stops.text: Cole Escola's Broadway comedy reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a would-be cabaret star. The national tour plays the Ahmanson through December 6, with Alaska Thunderfuck in the title role. The show runs 80 minutes with no intermission, so you'll be out by 8:30. Tickets start at about $60 with fees. Rush seats ($49 or $79, code MARYRUSH) go on sale online at 9 a.m. on the day of the show.

stay.name: Chateau Marmont
stay.text: The 1929 castle above Sunset Boulevard has 63 rooms, suites, cottages and bungalows, and Time Out calls its patio restaurant celebrated. It's on Time Out's April 2026 list of the best hotels in Los Angeles. This weekend it's also a short walk from the eastern end of Live on Sunset, so you can walk back to bed on Saturday night instead of looking for a car.

stay.name: Hotel Erwin Venice Beach
stay.text: A boutique hotel just off the Venice boardwalk. Many rooms have balconies facing the ocean, and Kassi, its Greek-inspired rooftop restaurant, is a good place for a drink at sunset. It's on Time Out's 2026 lists of the best hotels in the city and on the beach. Stay here to make Friday a walking day, then drive or take a rideshare inland for Saturday and Sunday.

stay.name: The LINE LA
stay.text: A 384-room hotel on Wilshire Boulevard with a pool, a karaoke bar and an Alfred Coffee in the lobby, and some of the lowest rates on Time Out's April 2026 list. Koreatown sits between the three days of this plan, about twenty minutes from Hollywood and downtown and on the Metro D Line. It's also surrounded by late-night Korean restaurants if you get hungry after a show.

events.name: LA Phil: Tchaikovsky's Fourth Symphony
events.where: Walt Disney Concert Hall, Bunker Hill
events.text: Jukka-Pekka Saraste conducts Sibelius's *The Bard*, Billy Childs's saxophone concerto *Diaspora* with Steven Banks, and Tchaikovsky's Fourth. A pre-concert talk is at 7 p.m. Tickets start at $44.

events.name: UCLA vs. Illinois
events.text: A Friday-night Big Ten game at the Rose Bowl, broadcast on FOX. Expect heavy traffic on the 110 and the 134 toward Pasadena in the early evening.

events.name: Live on Sunset
events.where: Sunset Blvd. between Doheny Dr. and San Vicente Blvd., West Hollywood
events.text: A free street concert with Sheryl Crow headlining, plus Local Natives, Empress Of and Grace Bowers. Registration is required. Sunset is closed to cars along this stretch from noon Friday to noon Sunday.

events.name: Camp Flog Gnaw Carnival
events.when: Sat. and Sun., noon to 11 p.m.
events.text: Tyler, the Creator's two-day festival, with Turnstile, Steve Lacy, Future and Don Toliver on the lineup. Expect traffic around Chinatown, Echo Park and the 110 both days.

events.name: Jorge Drexler
events.where: Walt Disney Concert Hall, Bunker Hill
events.text: The Uruguayan songwriter, who won an Oscar for "Al Otro Lado del Río", plays an acoustic concert of songs from across his career, including some from his album *Taracá*. Tickets start at $67.

events.name: MOCA: Julian Charrière and Cecilia Vicuña open
events.text: Opening day for *Deep End* and *Quipu of Encounters: The Dream of Water*, the first exhibitions for MOCA's Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize. General admission is free.

events.name: CicLAvia Pasadena
events.where: Colorado Blvd. and Raymond Ave., Pasadena
events.text: About 2.7 miles of Pasadena streets closed to cars and open to people on bikes and on foot, with a spur to the Metro A Line's Memorial Park station. It's free and you can join anywhere.

events.name: The Who's Tommy: closing weekend
events.when: Sun. 1 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. (Sat. 2 and 8 p.m.)
events.text: The touring revival of the Who's rock opera plays its last performances at the Pantages on Sunday.

know: **From LAX.** The FlyAway bus runs nonstop to Union Station downtown for $12.75 (about 45 minutes; pay by card or app). Rideshares and taxis pick up at the LAX-it lot next to Terminal 1. For Venice, a car from LAX takes about 20 minutes outside rush hour. Metro riders can take the free shuttle to the LAX/Metro Transit Center for the C and K lines.

**Metro.** A ride costs $1.75, with free transfers for two hours. Tapping a TAP card, a phone or a contactless bank card caps what you spend at $5 a day and $18 a week. The D Line serves Koreatown, and the A Line goes to Pasadena and to Little Tokyo/Arts District station.

**Sunset Strip closure.** Sunset Boulevard is closed to cars between San Vicente Boulevard and Doheny Drive from noon Friday until noon Sunday for Live on Sunset. Expect detours on Santa Monica Boulevard and in the hills, and use a rideshare or walk rather than driving to the Strip.

**Dodger Stadium and Pasadena.** Camp Flog Gnaw runs from noon to 11 p.m. on Saturday and Sunday at Dodger Stadium, so roads around Chinatown, Echo Park and the 110 will be slow. On Sunday, CicLAvia closes Colorado Boulevard in Pasadena to cars from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

**Weather and light.** As of Monday, Weather Underground forecast highs of about 78°F on Friday and 77°F on Saturday, with lows near 59°F, and showers on Sunday with a high near 72°F. Live on Sunset goes ahead rain or shine. The sun sets just before 5 p.m.
**Tipping.** Tip about 18 to 20 percent at sit-down restaurants and a dollar or two per drink at bars. Check the bill first, because some Los Angeles restaurants add a service charge.
